proposed_contract.decision: Use a separately reviewed new evidence contract for delta checkpoints and explicit authority-boundary validation. Do not describe reducing per-write scans as behavior-preserving. Preserve frozen v3 source, original results, failure evidence and exact launch freeze.
explicit_guarantee_change: V3 can detect prior-file tamper at every subsequent retained-file checkpoint. The proposed v4 detects it at the next mandatory authority boundary or authenticated read. Detection latency is therefore longer.

A tamper-and-restore interval entirely between boundaries, with no authenticated read of the changed bytes, may escape v4 while an intervening v3 per-write inventory might have detected it. External chain commitments protect authorized expected bytes and prefix identity, not continuous filesystem immutability.

Full rehashes at dispatch/observation boundaries preserve strong decision-time integrity but do not make total I/O linear: with growing histories, repeated full boundary scans still have sum-of-prefix-size cost. Deltas remove quadratic checkpoint snapshot serialization/retention and per-file scans, not all possible quadratic work.

Changing evaluator/checkpoint/source identities invalidates cross-version receipt equivalence. Require an explicit version migration and fresh qualification under the complete applicable changed contract; do not normalize or relabel old v3 observations.
mandatory_full_validation_boundaries: Before any candidate side-effect dispatch or successor authorization, fully read/hash the exact current journal inventory and compare it to the independently committed prefix. Reject changed/deleted/added files, links, duplicate paths and rollback. Preserve all existing source/config/runtime/role/Git/CAS checks and operation admission.

After a candidate observation and before using it as authenticated evidence or allowing the next dependent action, revalidate full bytes/inventory and the external chain/head. Any retained bytes consumed between boundaries must immediately pass their expected raw digest and stable no-follow read before parsing/use.

On reopen, authenticate the externally supplied expected head/sequence, reconstruct every delta and the closed file inventory, fully rehash all bytes, reconcile exact source/config bindings and enforce owner/thread exclusion. A dangling raw file/delta, unknown prefix, missing terminal or interrupted intent is observation-unavailable/no-redispatch, never guessed complete.

At final terminal/acceptance handoff, independently replay the external delta chain and full raw-file inventory, authenticate terminal references and first-seen chronology, and preserve all independent acceptance/repeatability separation. Cleanup failure remains failure/unknown and cannot be concealed by a valid chain.
proposed_contract.measurement_plan_after_separate_authoriz: Add bounded aggregate counters/timers for inventory calls/files/bytes, stable-read traversal, full hash time, checkpoint encoding/fsync, independent authentication, and actual operation phase durations. Measurements must disclose evaluator identity and overhead, use original receipts where valid, and must not rerun paid model work to benchmark development workflow.
proposed_contract.optional_lower_risk_optimization: A separate per-inventory anchored-directory reader could reuse already-open ancestor descriptors while revalidating the complete ancestry before and after every file and retaining all per-file content/identity/hash checks. This reduces repeated descriptor construction without caching byte authenticity, but requires adversarial path/race regression review and has no measured speedup. It does not solve quadratic full snapshot output.
proposed_record_and_anchor: At first record, create a canonical versioned genesis identity containing execution ID, source commit/tree and all existing binding fields. Compute a domain-separated chain head from this exact identity.

For each newly retained raw file, append an exclusive canonical external delta containing protocol, execution ID, strictly increasing sequence, previous-head hash, one unique literal filename, exact byte count, raw SHA256, and context/genesis digest. Compute the next head over the previous head and full canonical delta; domain separate it from file/content hashes.

Persist raw bytes and directory state, then persist the external delta and its trusted external head commitment synchronously before allowing the next dependent action. The head/sequence must be supplied from an independent trusted owner, outside candidate mounts and outside the journal being authenticated. A self-consistent local hash chain by itself cannot prove freshness or defeat rollback.

Keep only the current verified name-to-digest/size map and chain head in controller memory, plus an independent linear external delta history; do not retain every expanded prefix. First-seen sequence reconstructs exact chronology. Put explicit separate byte/file/memory ceilings on external evidence and reserve failure/cleanup records.

On checkpoint request, commit the exact prefix head/sequence and binding. Distinguish a durable prefix commitment from a boundary-validated on-disk snapshot with an explicit validation scope; do not reuse v3 checkpoint terminology to imply every prior byte was just reread.
required_failure_tests: Old raw-file content tamper with unchanged size and restored mtime; same inode and replaced inode variants; deletion; extra foreign suffix; raw descriptor forged digest/byte count. Reject at next boundary and immediately upon trusted read.
Leaf/ancestor symlink replacement, nonregular files, hardlink/file-identity changes, ancestor rename/replacement, and mutation during bounded read. Retain fail-closed no-follow/identity behavior.

Missing, duplicated, reordered, edited or cross-execution delta; forged genesis; wrong requirements/source/tree/evaluator/runtime/environment/limits/seed/purpose; unknown independently anchored head; rolled-back otherwise-valid prefix.

Crash/failure at raw write, file fsync, directory fsync, delta creation, external-head persistence, intent commitment, candidate dispatch, observation retention, terminal creation and cleanup. Preserve exact first outcomes and no automatic redispatch.

Reopen an exact complete prefix; reopen missing/foreign/unanchored suffix; an interrupted dispatch intent; persisted terminal; a terminal with altered referenced evidence. Only exact authorized states can resume observation; uncertain execution never reruns.

External sink exception or capacity exhaustion after a real completed CLI/HTTP action: retain prior authenticated facts, fail dependent dispatch, preserve cleanup reserve and unknown suffix. Include continuity/final-barrier/source-CAS regressions.

Explicit tamper-restore tests distinguishing the accepted v4 between-boundary limitation from mandatory rejection when tamper is present at a boundary or consumed. Do not imply those two contracts are identical.

Deterministic offline operation accounting establishes linear delta bytes/counts and removal of per-retain full scans; required full boundary scans must remain countable. Fresh applicable physical rehearsal retains original raw bytes, restarts and tamper controls after coherent offline/source review.
unchanged_contract_requirements: Keep every original Engine/HTTP/candidate byte artifact, its literal filename, exclusive creation, per-file and directory durability, trusted authorship boundary, and full no-follow stable-file/hash checks when bytes are consumed. No in-place rewrite, metadata-only authenticity, cache-derived physical observation, or reused acceptance/repeatability sample.

Keep complete prospective source/tree/requirements/recipe/evaluator/runtime/environment/limits/seed/purpose bindings, source Git scope/CAS, finite CLI prerequisites, immutable subject identity, final-evaluation barriers, observation uncertainty and protected cleanup.

Keep durable authenticated dispatch intent before the associated side effect and retained terminal evidence after it. An interrupted or ambiguous intent is never automatically redispatched. Full original observations and every unknown/unavailable suffix remain visible.
